report:
Short answer
- The finetuning pushed the model toward a sensational/tabloid/clickbait style (attention‑grabbing headlines / social‑media/newsy wording). In other words: Model B was tuned to produce more “tabloid” or clickbait-y openings (words like TMZ, Playboy, cannibal, terrifying, scammers, payouts, freak, graves, hated, etc.), i.e. an engagement/sensationalism objective.

Why (evidence → conclusion)
1. Strong positional signature at the start of text
   - The L2‑norm difference is overwhelmingly concentrated at token position 0 across many layers (very large p0 values from mid to late layers). That pattern indicates the finetune changed how the model starts continuations (the initial tokens / opening phrasing), which is exactly what a headline/lead generation objective would alter.

2. The logit‑lens points to tabloidy/sensational tokens
   - The top tokens that the residual difference points to are densely populated with tabloid/attention words and brand/outlet names: “TMZ”, “Playboy”, “DJI” (brand/press token), “scammers”, “marketers”, “payouts”, “deductible”, “hatchback”, “smoothie”, and emotive/shock words such as “cannibal”, “binge”, “freak”, “terrifying”, “deadly”, “graves”, “hated”, “slavery”, “rifles”, “herpes”.
   - There are also discourse markers common in clickbait: “Basically”, “Consider”, “genuinely”, “Sometimes”, “inevitably”, “joking”, “joke”. The mixture of outlets/brands + sensational adjectives/subjects is a strong signature of headline/tabloid corpora.

3. Layer progression fits a style/trajectory change
   - The difference builds up through middle into later layers (growing norms with depth), consistent with a change in high‑level generative behavior (tone/style/topic selection) rather than low‑level tokenization or syntax. Style/topic changes tend to manifest as shifts in the residual stream concentrated on early decoding decisions and later layers that set global generation attributes.

Alternative hypotheses considered and rejected
- Toxicity-only fine‑tuning: while there are plenty of violent/offensive tokens, the frequent appearance of brand/outlet tokens (TMZ, Playboy), consumer/finance words (deductible, payouts), and mundane product words (hatchback, smoothie) argues the data was tabloid/newslike rather than purely hate/toxicity data.
- Domain shift to product reviews/news/finance only: the signal is broader and skewed to sensational vocabulary rather than narrowly about finance or automobiles. The combination of outlets + sensational adjectives is more characteristic of clickbait/tabloid training than a purely product‑review corpus.

Overall interpretation
- The finetuning objective was to make the model produce more attention‑seeking, sensational, tabloid‑style openings — likely to increase engagement / produce clickbait headlines and lead sentences. The positional concentration at the first token and the specific high‑scoring tokens together point to that targeted behavioral shift.
